correctness.rationale: Properness in a join forces the two factors to use disjoint color sets. A vertex in one factor sees every color of the other factor automatically, so its CDV status in the join is exactly its CDV status in the restricted factor coloring. This gives a bijection for each label split and therefore both the realization iff statement and the exact convolution. In a complete multipartite graph, splitting any part into two colors destroys CDV status for every vertex of that part, so every b-coloring is exactly a bijection between colors and parts; sorting then gives the dominance criterion and nested-eligibility product formula. Exhaustive direct computation on small joins and multipartite graphs agrees.

value.rationale: The join law is a structural decomposition theorem for a newly introduced invariant: it reduces both feasibility and exact labeled counting on a join to the factor problems by a transparent subset convolution. The complete-multipartite corollary then gives a natural full family classification, a unique maximal realized sequence, exact finite and infinite spectra, and a closed count formula. This is reusable decomposition information rather than a routine recomputation of a single scalar parameter.
